projects.title: BLADE: Botanical Leaf Analysis & Disease Evaluator
projects.result: A handheld, fully offline crop-disease scanner. Paper under review.
bullets: Built on a Raspberry Pi 4B with a 5 MP camera, a touchscreen interface and a custom 3D-printed enclosure. A pretrained MobileNetV2 convolutional neural network classifies a leaf photo into 38 classes (26 diseases, 12 healthy states) across 14 crops.

The pipeline runs input checks, combines five augmented views of each image (test-time augmentation) and applies confidence thresholds, so the device answers "uncertain" rather than giving a wrong diagnosis.
I rebuilt the device (camera swap, reworked internal layout, full software audit, Git version control, speed optimization) and redesigned the study as a controlled experiment.

**Research question:** why do plant-disease models that score ~99% on lab images fail in real fields? Is the cause the leaf or the background? BLADE photographs the same leaves while changing one condition at a time (background, framing, lighting), which turns a correlation found in earlier studies into a controlled test.

technicalIntro: How each system works, the design decisions behind it, what broke and what we changed, and exactly what I did.

technicalProjects.name: The Orca
technicalProjects.summary: Our 2026 underwater ROV, built in about two months for ~$600, against rival budgets of $15,000–20,000.
subsystems: The manipulator is a single-motor gripper. Its gripping surface is a kitchen sponge combined with M-seal epoxy putty, and we replaced the putty after every run.

A Pixhawk 2.4.8 flight controller runs ArduSub (Sub V4.5.7), configured in Mission Planner 1.3.83 for the vectored 6-DOF frame (FRAME_CONFIG = 2) and its six thrusters. We flashed the Pixhawk using Mission Planner's Force Bootloader option.
A NEMO-style vertical profiling float changes depth with a syringe-based buoyancy engine, with a DC-thruster version as the backup. It runs on an ESP32 and communicates over ESP-NOW.

decisions.decision: Sponge plus M-seal epoxy putty as the gripping surface
decisions.why: 3D-printed jaws, sponge alone and putty alone each failed underwater.
decisions.tradeoff: The putty had to be replaced after every run.

decisions.decision: A DC-thruster version of the float's buoyancy engine as backup
decisions.why: A second way to drive the float if the syringe engine failed.

changes: Manipulator: we planned a worm-gear jaw with wrist rotation, then dropped it for time and built the single-motor gripper instead.
Servo waterproofing stayed a recurring problem: too much sealant jammed the gears, and too little let water in.
Float link: we replaced the float's earlier Bluetooth link with ESP-NOW.
myRole: As Arm Design Lead, designed and built The Orca's single-motor gripper.

technicalProjects.name: BLADE
technicalProjects.subtitle: Botanical Leaf Analysis & Disease Evaluator
technicalProjects.summary: A handheld, fully offline crop-disease scanner that classifies a leaf photo, or answers "uncertain" instead of guessing.
subsystems: A Raspberry Pi 4B with a 5 MP OV5647 camera, a touchscreen GUI and a battery, in a custom 3D-printed enclosure. Everything runs offline.

Input checks run first: a plant-colour check, an object filter, and a face/privacy filter. A pretrained MobileNetV2 (trained on PlantVillage) then classifies the leaf into 38 classes (26 diseases, 12 healthy states) across 14 crops, combining five augmented views of each image (test-time augmentation). Confidence and margin thresholds decide whether to show a diagnosis or answer "uncertain". Every scan is logged to a spreadsheet.

The study photographs the same physical leaves while changing one variable at a time: background, framing and lighting. It compares lab-to-field accuracy (PlantVillage → PlantDoc) and measures image statistics: colour saturation, border edge density and leaf fill fraction.

decisions.decision: Confidence and margin thresholds that can answer "uncertain"
decisions.why: A wrong diagnosis is worse than no diagnosis.
decisions.tradeoff: Some scans end without a diagnosis.

decisions.decision: Input checks before the model sees the image
decisions.why: Only plant images reach the classifier, and the face filter protects privacy.

decisions.decision: Five augmented views per image (test-time augmentation)
decisions.tradeoff: Five model passes per scan instead of one.

changes: The original camera's board shifted inside the case. I swapped the camera and reworked the internal layout.
I ran a full software audit and put the code under Git version control with a restore point.
Speed: I added per-stage timing, moved logging to the background and batched inference. Quantized TFLite is in progress.
myRole: Rebuilt the device: camera swap and a reworked internal layout.
Audited the software, added Git version control, instrumented per-stage timing and optimized speed.
Redesigned the study as a controlled experiment.

technicalProjects.name: WRO Future Engineers self-driving car
task: The car must be fully autonomous: no remote control, and radios and Wi-Fi off during runs. It starts with a single button press.
The arena is a 3 × 3 m track with walls. **Open Challenge:** 3 laps with a randomized driving direction, starting position and inner-wall placement, without touching the walls.

**Obstacle Challenge:** 3 laps around red and green pillars (pass red on the right, green on the left). The last pillar of lap 2 decides whether lap 3 continues or reverses direction. Then the car finds a magenta-marked parking lot and parallel parks. Moving a pillar costs points, and each run has a 3-minute limit.
Vehicle limits: 300 × 200 × 300 mm and 1.5 kg; four wheels, one driving axle and one steering actuator. Car-style steering is required; differential-drive steering is banned.
specs: Lego (2024) · custom, from an RC truck (2025)
subsystems: Python with OpenCV colour detection finds the red and green pillars, using contour analysis and size-threshold filtering.
Ackermann steering and a rear drive motor. 2024 used a store-bought Lego differential; in 2025 we built a custom differential from a disassembled RC truck and its single large motor.

decisions.why: The rules require car-style steering with one steering actuator; differential-drive steering is banned.

decisions.decision: Contour analysis with size-threshold filtering on colour detections
decisions.why: Pillars are identified by colour, and the size threshold drops detections too small to be a pillar.

changes: 2024 → 2025: replaced the store-bought Lego differential with a custom differential built from a disassembled RC truck and its single large motor.
Duct tape proved too weak to hold the custom differential, so a teammate modelled custom structural supports in CAD.
myRole: 2024 (team member): mostly physical work, including soldering and testing.
2025 (team lead): led the 3-person team through the custom-differential rebuild.
Did most of the design and strategy for the 2025 car.
